I read the whole target file. I also read RationalHeightLE in Estimates/RationalHeight.lean and scaledPairAssemble, scaledPairLayer and scaledPairLayerEquiv in Geometry/DilationPairCoordinates.lean.

The hypotheses are jointly satisfiable. Examples include Q = P = ⊥ with empty bases, and any nested pair of subspaces with rational coordinate bases of height at most H. Nothing forces an empty domain.

The conclusion is not trivial. It gives a genuine basis of the layer, indexed by Fin (finrank), whose pair coordinates both have height at most H*K. The two kinds of basis vector have the expected heights:
- For a Q-basis vector a_j, the image under scaledPairLayerEquiv is (a_j, 0). Its coordinates have height at most H, and the zero coordinate has height at most 1 ≤ H.
- For a P-basis vector b_j, the image is (q•b_j, b_j). The first coordinate has height at most K*H, and the second has height at most H.

The assumption 1 ≤ H is needed only for the zero coordinates. 1 ≤ K is needed only for H ≤ H*K. Both are mild and appropriate. The edge cases q = 0 and empty α or β are handled correctly. The Fintype assumptions make the finrank indexing valid.

I found no vacuity or mismatch with the intended purpose. I have no uncertainty about the mathematics.
